finding: Independent review identified that try_wait bounds child exit but wait_with_output can still wait indefinitely for pipe EOF retained by another process.

effectiveCounterexample.method: The actual run_isolated_command helper reaped a controlled shell while its background child held stdout/stderr open at an owned FIFO gate. Capture remained blocked until gate release.

fix: Use two anonymous tempfile files for stdout/stderr, cloning handles only for the controlled child.
After child exit, read at most 64 KiB using FileExt::read_exact_at. This neither waits for writer closure nor moves the shared file offset.
Retain successful exit and exact completion-token checks.
Regression requires holder-opened and absence of holder-completed before accepting capture success. Afterwards it releases the owned gate and observes completion; read has an 8-second fallback.

ownedProcessObservation.method: Read-only ps match anchored to the actual /bin/sh executable and exact controlled script/argument; excludes parent shell command text. No name-based kill.

limits: Only test harness changed. Production stdio and XLSX source were not changed.

The background holder is a shell grandchild. Its completion marker proves the final statement before shell exit, not waitpid/reap by this test. The direct primary child is reaped through its Child handle.
8-second read fallback plus explicit gate release bounds this controlled holder. A read-only process snapshot found no matching holder command after the final run.
64 KiB is a logical capture limit, not an OS-level I/O timing guarantee.
Prior full-check receipts retain their actual source hashes. Root will run the final Rust/format checks for this test-only increment.
